An implementation that drops any one input (a common 'simplification' -- hashing only path plus label) collapses at least one variant onto the baseline.

rule_statement: Node identity MUST hash `path :: location :: kind :: normalized-label`.
notes: The `different_kind` variant differs from the baseline ONLY in intent kind (decision vs assumption) -- same path, same location, same label. An implementation that omits intent kind from the hash returns the SAME id for both, merging a decision node with the assumption it stated. Any output where distinct_count < 6 MUST be rejected.

rule_statement: The canonical source path MUST be repository-relative and POSIX-separated.
notes: An ABSOLUTE path to a record inside a repository MUST canonicalize to its repository-relative POSIX spelling. Substitute a real repository root for `<REPO_ROOT>` when running this fixture. This is what makes an identity reproducible across clones: hashing the absolute spelling makes every node id machine-specific, so the same record ingested via an absolute path forks the node a relative re-ingest produces.

rule_statement: The canonical source path MUST be repository-relative and POSIX-separated.
notes: An ALREADY-relative path MUST come through unchanged apart from separator normalization. An implementation that resolves every input to an absolute path first (then back to relative) forks the ids of every existing relative-built graph. Any output other than the input string MUST be rejected.

rule_statement: A path outside a repository falls back to POSIX absolute; canonicalization MUST NOT raise.
notes: An absolute path belonging to no repository MUST fall back to a POSIX-normalized absolute spelling rather than raising or returning empty.

rule_statement: A path outside a repository falls back to POSIX absolute; canonicalization MUST NOT raise.
notes: A path containing a NUL byte. REC-074 states canonicalization MUST NOT raise, so a conformant implementation returns SOME string (or declines the path through its normal absent-value channel) rather than propagating an exception. DIVERGENCE: v0.8.3 propagates ValueError('embedded null byte') from the underlying path resolution. Path spellings arrive from tool-call arguments and configuration, so this is a reachable trust boundary, not a theoretical one. The `expect` below states the SPEC-required outcome.

expect.divergence: REC-074's 'MUST NOT raise' is not honoured: a NUL byte in an absolute path propagates ValueError out of canonical_source_path(). `expect` states the SPECIFICATION's requirement; the `engine_*` keys are the behaviour observed at v0.8.3. A harness run against the reference implementation MUST expect the engine_* values and record the divergence -- it MUST NOT rewrite the conformance target to match.

rule_statement: A record MUST be a UTF-8 markdown document.
notes: The file contains the bytes 0xFF 0xFE, which begin no valid UTF-8 sequence, so it is not a UTF-8 document and therefore not a conformant record. Read this fixture as RAW BYTES, not as text. DIVERGENCE: the v0.8.3 reference reads record files with `encoding='utf-8-sig', errors='replace'`, so the undecodable bytes become U+FFFD and the file is ingested as a record whose rationale silently differs from the bytes on disk. The `expect` below states the SPEC-required outcome.

expect.engine_note: ingest_dir() ingests the file with replacement characters in the rationale
expect.divergence: REC-002 has no reject branch in v0.8.3: undecodable bytes are replaced with U+FFFD rather than the file being rejected as a non-conformant record. `expect` states the SPECIFICATION's requirement; the `engine_*` keys are the behaviour observed at v0.8.3. A harness run against the reference implementation MUST expect the engine_* values and record the divergence -- it MUST NOT rewrite the conformance target to match.

rule_statement: `**Status:**` and `**Date:**` MUST be emitted on adjacent lines after the H1.
notes: The two metadata lines MUST be ADJACENT -- line 2 and line 3, with no blank line between them. An emitter that separates them with a blank line (a natural markdown-prettifying instinct) produces the non-conformant output shown. Adjacency is what lets a reader treat the pair as one metadata block rather than two stray bold lines.

rule_statement: A slug MUST be bounded at 60 characters.
notes: The source question is well over 60 characters. The slug MUST be at most 60. An implementation that omits the bound produces the non-conformant slug shown -- a filename long enough to trip path-length limits on some filesystems, and unreadable in a directory listing.

rule_statement: A first word exceeding the bound MUST be hard-cut -- the only permitted mid-word cut.
notes: The first word is 61 characters -- one over the bound -- so there is no earlier `-` to truncate at. The slug MUST be hard-cut to 60. An implementation that returns the whole first word because 'the word-boundary rule found no boundary' emits the 61-character non-conformant slug shown, leaving the slug unbounded exactly when the bound matters most.

rule_statement: An empty slug MUST become the literal `decision`.
notes: The source text is whitespace only, so the derived slug reduces to the empty string and MUST become the literal `decision`. An implementation returning '' produces the filename '<date>-.md' -- and every question that slugs to nothing then collides on that one name, which is the REC-056 overwrite class returning through a different door.

rule_statement: A slug MUST NOT be able to contain a glob metacharacter.
notes: The positive control for REC-063: an ordinary question produces a slug drawn only from [a-z0-9-]. This is the property REC-068's lookup pattern is built on -- the slug is interpolated directly into a glob, so it must never be able to contribute a metacharacter.

rule_statement: Otherwise the destination MUST be `<today>-<question-slug>.md`.
notes: An empty records directory: no legacy name and no existing dated record, so neither REC-064 nor REC-067 applies and the destination is minted fresh. It MUST be `<today>-` followed by the slug of the QUESTION -- note the filename carries nothing from the chosen option ('Shard the primary'), which is REC-056's whole point.

rule_statement: Otherwise the destination MUST be `<today>-<question-slug>.md`.
notes: An empty records directory and an EMPTY question. The question slug of an empty string is the literal `decision` (REC-062), so REC-069 requires `2026-07-25-decision.md`. DIVERGENCE: v0.8.3 substitutes the CHOSEN option for an empty question before slugging (`slugify(question.strip() or chosen)`) and emits `2026-07-25-keep-the-window.md` -- a chosen-derived filename, which is precisely the collision class REC-056 exists to kill. Two captures with no question that happen to choose the same words would land on the same file. The spec does not describe this fallback at all: either REC-069 must state it, or the implementation must drop it.

expect.divergence: REC-069 has an undocumented empty-question fallback: the destination slug is derived from the CHOSEN option, not the question, whenever the question is empty. `expect` states the SPECIFICATION's requirement; the `engine_*` keys are the behaviour observed at v0.8.3. A harness run against the reference implementation MUST expect the engine_* values and record the divergence -- it MUST NOT rewrite the conformance target to match.
